questions.text: Which starting point is source-safe for HVAC system selection under the checked DOE family?

options.text: Determine cooling loads using accepted methods and local design conditions before selecting equipment.
Select equipment first, then calculate loads only if space remains.
Use the same tonnage for every building of the same height.
Base selection only on the color of the outdoor unit.

questions.rationale: The checked DOE family directs designers to use accepted load-calculation methods and indoor/outdoor design conditions.
questions.code_citation: LEA-UTIL-002-04 Module Cooling Load Estimation; ASHRAE 90.1 solar gain factors; PD 1096 (National Building Code) / RA 9514 (Fire Code)

questions.text: Which DOE sizing principle best fits large central HVAC plants?

options.text: Size close to the calculated load and consider multiple units or staging for part-load operation.
Oversize all chillers because part-load operation is not a design concern.
Ignore future load reductions from envelope and lighting measures.
Operate all chillers continuously regardless of demand.

questions.rationale: The DOE guideline discusses sizing close to load, considering load reductions, using multiple chiller units, and managing part-load operation.
questions.code_citation: PD 1096 Rule VII Section 704; ASHRAE 378; LEA-UTIL-002-04 Module Commissioning Checklist

questions.text: What source-safe role do controls and VSDs play in HVAC selection?

options.text: They support energy-efficient operation through monitoring, variable-speed fans, pumps, and zone controls where appropriate.
They replace the need for load calculations.
They are forbidden for HVAC systems in buildings.
They apply only to architectural finishes.

questions.rationale: The checked DOE family supports monitoring/control, fan VSDs, pumping control, and zone/duct control as part of HVAC energy design.
questions.code_citation: LEA-UTIL-002-04 Module VRF Systems section; ASHRAE efficiency data; tropical climate operation patterns

questions.text: Which LEA statement is source-safe when comparing room units and central systems?

options.text: Room units can serve limited rooms, while central chilled-water and air-handling systems suit larger coordinated building loads.
Window units are always the correct choice for every building scale.
Central cooling never needs air handling or chilled-water coordination.
The system type is independent of load, scale, and operation.

questions.rationale: The checked Salvan family discusses window or through-the-wall room units and central cooling with chilled water and air-handling coordination.
